freeCopyCases: One free set of copies per provider for an indigent person when the records support a Social Security Act claim or appeal (W. Va. Code 16-29-2(f), (g))
feeRules: Patient or personal representative: no more than a fee consistent with HIPAA, plus applicable taxes (16-29-2(a))
Other requesters: search and handling fee up to $20, 40 cents per paper page, plus postage and taxes (16-29-2(b)(1))
Electronic copies for other requesters: up to 20 cents per page, capped at $150 inclusive of all fees (16-29-2(b)(2))

provisions.title: Reasonable expenses to be reimbursed (free copy for Social Security claims)
provisions.quote: a provider shall not impose a charge on an indigent person or his or her authorized representative if the medical records are necessary for the purpose of supporting a claim or appeal under any provisions of the Social Security Act
provisions.appliesTo: A provider; indigent person as defined in 16-29-2(f)(1)-(2); "limited to one set of copies per provider"

provisions.title: Reasonable expenses to be reimbursed (patient fee rule)
provisions.quote: A provider may charge a patient or the patient’s personal representative no more than a fee consistent with HIPAA
provisions.appliesTo: A provider; patient or personal representative

provisions.title: Copies of health care records to be furnished to patients
provisions.quote: within no more than thirty days from the receipt of the request, furnish a copy
provisions.appliesTo: A health care provider so licensed, certified or registered under the laws of this state

copy_rights.note: Deadline is 30 days, equal to HIPAA, so it does not count. The free copy for an indigent Social Security claim or appeal goes beyond HIPAA and 45 CFR 171.302. One element in force.

crossCheck.note: Free copy for an indigent person's Social Security claim or appeal is a benefits-claim case beyond HIPAA and 45 CFR 171.302. The 30-day deadline equals HIPAA. HB 3311 (2021) and 2025 bill 2402 dates confirmed.

provisions.title: WVHIN For Patients page (opt-out policy)
provisions.citation: WVHIN patient FAQ and opt-out form
provisions.quote: Yes, patients can choose not to make their data available in WVHIN. This is called opting-out.
provisions.appliesTo: Patients whose providers participate in WVHIN; opt-out form at connect.wvhin.org/optoutform

provisions.title: WVHIN For Patients page (substance use treatment records)
provisions.quote: Federal rules say that an addiction treatment provider needs your consent before they share information about your addiction treatment.
provisions.appliesTo: Addiction treatment provider records exchanged through WVHIN

provisions.title: West Virginia Health Information Network; privacy; protection of information
provisions.quote: The Health Care Authority shall ensure that patient specific protected health information be disclosed only in accordance with the patient's authorization or best interest to those having a need to know
provisions.appliesTo: The West Virginia Health Information Network

leads.usedFor: Located the WVHIN patient pages and opt-out form

hie_consent.note: Statute 16-29G-8 allows disclosure by authorization or best interest and sets no opt-in. WVHIN policy is opt-out. Health.wv.gov says WVHIN serves as the state's HIE. Effective date is the page's last modified date. Sensitive flag rests on federal Part 2.

crossCheck.note: Basis is WVHIN policy, page modified 2026-07-09, with an online opt-out form. 16-29G-8 (effective 2006-06-07) sets no opt-in. Sensitive flag rests on the page's addiction treatment consent statement.

provisions.title: Reports of abortions
provisions.quote: Individual records may only be released for research purposes as approved by the state Registrar and may be released in a format designed to further protect the confidentiality of the woman as the state Registrar deems necessary.
provisions.appliesTo: Abortion reports filed with the section of vital registration

reproductive.note: The rule covers abortion reports held by vital registration. Reports must omit personal identifiers. No separate rule for provider-held reproductive records was found.

crossCheck.note: Latest signed amendment is HB 3199 (2023), effective from passage March 11, 2023. HB 4978 (2024) is listed on the page but was not enacted. The rule covers abortion reports filed with vital registration.

provisions.title: Definition of confidential information; disclosure
provisions.quote: Confidential information shall not be disclosed, except: (1) In a proceeding under §27-5-4 of this code to disclose the results of an involuntary examination made pursuant to §27-5-2, §27-5-3, or §27-5-4
provisions.appliesTo: Communications and information obtained in the course of treatment or evaluation of any client or patient (Chapter 27)

leads.usedFor: Search result pointing to Chapter 27 Article 3 consent rules

mental_health.note: Chapter 27 Article 3 lists the cases where treatment information may be disclosed, including court orders.

crossCheck.note: SB 543 (2018) effective June 5, 2018, matches the researcher's date. The section lists the cases in which treatment information may be disclosed.

provisions.title: Confidentiality of records; permitted disclosure
provisions.quote: No person may disclose or be compelled to disclose the identity of any person upon whom an HIV-related test is performed, or the results of such a test in a manner which permits identification of the subject of the test
provisions.appliesTo: Any person; HIV-related test identity and results

hiv.note: Disclosure is allowed only to listed persons, including anyone holding a specific release signed by the test subject.

crossCheck.note: SB 488 (2011) effective June 10, 2011, matches. Listed recipients include a person who secures a specific release executed by the test subject.

facts.statutoryDamages: HIV test law: liquidated damages of $1,000 (reckless) or $10,000 (intentional or malicious), or actual damages if greater, plus attorney fees (16-3C-5)

provisions.title: Remedies and penalties (HIV-related testing)
provisions.quote: Any person aggrieved by a violation of this article has right of action in the circuit court and may recover for the violation
provisions.appliesTo: Violations of Article 3C (AIDS-related medical testing and records confidentiality)

provisions.title: Copies of health care records to be furnished to patients (enforcement)
provisions.quote: The provisions of this article may be enforced by a patient, personal representative, authorized agent or authorized representative.
provisions.appliesTo: Access to copies under Article 29 only

private_right.note: Private right limited to HIV test records (16-3C-5). The Article 29 enforcement right covers access to copies, not unlawful disclosure. Breach law enforcement is by the Attorney General only (46A-2A-104).

crossCheck.note: Private right limited to HIV test records. 1988 HB 303 enrolled text says in effect September 1, 1988. Damages $1,000 or $10,000 liquidated, or actual if greater. 16-29-1(c) covers copy access only.

provisions.title: Definitions (personal information)
provisions.quote: when the data elements are neither encrypted nor redacted: (A) Social security number; (B) Driver's license number or state identification card number issued in lieu of a driver's license; or (C) Financial account number
provisions.appliesTo: Individuals and entities that own or license computerized data that includes personal information

provisions.title: Notice of breach of security of computerized personal information
provisions.quote: the notice shall be made without unreasonable delay
provisions.appliesTo: An individual or entity that owns or licenses computerized data that includes personal information

provisions.title: Procedures deemed in compliance with security breach notice requirements
provisions.quote: An entity that complies with the notification requirements or procedures pursuant to the rules, regulation, procedures or guidelines established by the entity's primary or functional regulator shall be in compliance with this article.
provisions.appliesTo: Any entity with a primary or functional regulator

breach_health.note: Personal information covers SSN, license and financial account numbers only. No AG notice; notice to consumer reporting agencies over 1,000 persons. HIPAA is not named; a general primary-regulator compliance clause exists.
